messages:
leah_cs: Heads-up — Mosaic (acct mosaic-ai) hit a safety filtering inconsistency today that blocks otherwise-safe responses intermittently. Customer blocked in production, asked for ETA. Copying @sam_engineering and @mike_product for triage.

leah_cs: Repro steps I followed (from their support case):
```
1) API: POST /v1/generate
2) model: redwood-llama-13b-q4 (hosted)
3) payload:
{
  \"messages\": [
    {\"role\": \"system\", \"content\": \"You are a helpful assistant.\"},
    {\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"Summarize the following legal clause: [long clause text omitted].\"}
  ],
  \"temperature\": 0.2,
  \"safety_strictness\": \"default\"
}
```
Observed: sometimes the response returns full summary, sometimes returns a single-blocked token with message: \"Content blocked by safety filter\". Happens ~40% of requests. Customer ran this with same request_id across regions and saw variance.

leah_cs: Attached debug id from customer: debug-ctx-20260321-9f3a. Logs: 
- upstream status: 200
- body: {\"error\": \"policy_block\", \"reason\": \"safety:partial\", \"blocked_fragment\": \"<omitted>\"}

sam_engineering: Thanks, leah. A couple quick asks: can you confirm if they hit dedicated or hosted? and whether the requests used streaming vs non-streaming?

leah_cs: They are on hosted; non-streaming. I confirmed request headers: X-Region: us-west-2, model_binding: stable-2026-03. Customer says toggling temperature doesn't change frequency.

sam_engineering: Ok. My initial hypothesis: inconsistent safety outcome could be a) model variant drift between kernel selection paths (quantized path vs fallback), b) asynchronous policy evaluation race when streaming off, or c) cached KV prefix mismatch.

mike_product: :warning: Customer-impacting. Mosaic is in pilot and blocked for a core flow. Propose we triage as P1 for blocking customers. If eng confirms regression, we should consider temporary routing to a more conservative safety profile for their org (policy override) until fix. Thoughts?

olivia_sre: FYI operations: we can patch a per-org policy toggle via control plane in ~2-3 hours, but we need ENG sign-off to avoid side effects.

travis_support: Ticket #2345 opened with customer; they flagged this as Severity: high and need a workaround. They requested ETA and whether there is a config change we can apply.

sam_engineering: I'll pick this up. Next steps for me: 1) try to reproduce locally with same model version and quantization; 2) run request against staging vs prod to see variance; 3) inspect policy evaluation logs for debug-ctx-20260321-9f3a. If I can reproduce, I'll create an ENG issue and add detailed root-cause notes.

sam_engineering: Quick ask for leah: can you attach the raw response bodies (customer redacts PII) and the full request_id list? the one debug id helps but we need 3-5 examples showing pass vs block.

leah_cs: Uploaded three request_ids to the support ticket: req-8811, req-8817, req-8823. Raw bodies attached (redacted) and timestamped. Also included the exact customer prompt and model metadata.

triage-bot: Created ENG ticket INF-3781: https://redwood.internal/infra/INF-3781 — title: \"Inconsistent safety filter outcomes for hosted redwood-llama-13b-q4\". Linked support #2345, priority: P1 (pending eng triage).

sam_engineering: Thanks. I'll update INF-3781 with repro steps and earliest-failure stack traces. If this is a kernel-selection bug, might be a medium complexity fix. Will estimate after I reproduce.

mike_product: Please also include customer impact in ticket body (pilot revenue + blocked features). We should schedule a stakeholder sync after initial RCA.

leah_cs: Noted — added impact blurb to the ENG ticket and pinged customer success manager. Customer asked for a temporary mitigation; can ops patch the per-org policy if engineering agrees?

olivia_sre: We can hold off until eng confirms scope. If eng requests a stopgap, we can push a policy override and monitor.

sam_engineering: If I confirm inconsistency, ops mitigation sounds good. For tracking — I'll add a checklist in INF-3781: reproduce, isolate (kernel vs policy), create fix branch, QA test, canary, roll.

travis_support: Customer awaiting ETA. Any initial guess on timeline?

sam_engineering: No firm ETA yet. If I can reproduce today, aim to have a hotfix candidate within 48-72 hours; otherwise we'll need more investigation time. I'll update ticket and this thread. :+1:

leah_cs: Thanks all. I'll keep customer updated and escalate if they push.

sam_engineering: Quick debugging note for reviewers: run the repro with both model path flags:
```bash
# quantized path
REDWOOD_MODEL=redwood-llama-13b-q4 REDWOOD_KERNEL=quant ./run_repro.sh req-8811
# fallback path
REDWOOD_MODEL=redwood-llama-13b-q4 REDWOOD_KERNEL=fallback ./run_repro.sh req-8811
```
This helps confirm if kernel selection changes output.

leah_cs: Added those run commands to ticket. Closing loop for now — ping me if you need more artifacts. :wave:
